text: Before long. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice had become. <break time="0.8s" /> One of the most popular girls at the club. <break time="0.8s" /> And even Warren began. <break time="0.8s" /> To seek her out at every dance. <break time="0.8s" /> He listened to her stories eagerly. <break time="0.8s" /> And he seemed to have forgotten. <break time="0.8s" /> The long devotion. <break time="0.8s" /> He had once shown to Marjorie herself. <break time="0.8s" /> Marjorie had never truly wanted Warren. <break time="0.8s" /> But now that her cousin. <break time="0.8s" /> Was winning him away. <break time="0.8s" /> She watched them together. <break time="0.8s" /> With growing, silent resentment. <break time="0.8s" /> It was one thing. <break time="0.8s" /> To create a popular girl. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of a dull cousin. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was quite another. <break time="0.8s" /> To see that girl steal her own admirer. <break time="0.8s" /> One afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> In front of a group of their friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Marjorie remarked sweetly. <break time="0.8s" /> That Bernice had only been bluffing. <break time="0.8s" /> About cutting her hair. <break time="0.8s" /> Every eye turned to Bernice. <break time="0.8s" /> And she realized with a sinking heart. <break time="0.8s" /> That if she refused now. <break time="0.8s" /> All her new popularity. <break time="0.8s" /> Would disappear at once. <break time="0.8s" /> So she rose to her feet. <break time="0.8s" /> And walked to the barbershop. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the Sevier Hotel. <break time="0.8s" /> Followed by a curious, chattering crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> Of her friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking with her head held high. <break time="0.8s" /> She felt like Marie Antoinette. <break time="0.8s" /> On her way to the guillotine. <break time="0.8s" /> Determined not to show Marjorie her fear.
